#                             = dot(vec(v,p), vec(v,r))   (sign core)
#   Denominators:
#     angle_cos_den(p,v,r) = distance_sq(v,p)*distance_sq(v,r)
#     angle_cos_den(q,v,s) = distance_sq(v,q)*distance_sq(v,s)
#   Since |vq| = |vp| and |vs| = |vr|, the denominators agree.
#   Hence numerators squared times opposite denominators agree, and the signs
#   of the numerators agree. That is exactly are_angles_congruent.

thm vertical_angles_equal:
    ? forall p, q, r, s, v cart(R, R):
        q(1) = 2 * v(1) - p(1),
        q(2) = 2 * v(2) - p(2),
        s(1) = 2 * v(1) - r(1),
        s(2) = 2 * v(2) - r(2),
        distance_sq(v, p) > 0,
        distance_sq(v, r) > 0
        =>:
            $are_angles_congruent(p, v, r, q, v, s)
    # Declare vec expansions.
    vec(v, p) = (p(1) - v(1), p(2) - v(2))
    vec(v, r) = (r(1) - v(1), r(2) - v(2))
    vec(v, q) = (q(1) - v(1), q(2) - v(2))
    vec(v, s) = (s(1) - v(1), s(2) - v(2))
    # Reflection relations: vq = -vp and vs = -vr componentwise.
    q(1) - v(1) = (2 * v(1) - p(1)) - v(1)
    (2 * v(1) - p(1)) - v(1) = v(1) - p(1)
    v(1) - p(1) = -(p(1) - v(1))
    q(2) - v(2) = (2 * v(2) - p(2)) - v(2)
    (2 * v(2) - p(2)) - v(2) = v(2) - p(2)
    v(2) - p(2) = -(p(2) - v(2))
    s(1) - v(1) = (2 * v(1) - r(1)) - v(1)
    (2 * v(1) - r(1)) - v(1) = v(1) - r(1)
    v(1) - r(1) = -(r(1) - v(1))
    s(2) - v(2) = (2 * v(2) - r(2)) - v(2)
    (2 * v(2) - r(2)) - v(2) = v(2) - r(2)
    v(2) - r(2) = -(r(2) - v(2))
    # Numerator for angle pvr.
    angle_cos_num(p, v, r) = dot(vec(v, p), vec(v, r))
    dot(vec(v, p), vec(v, r)) = (p(1) - v(1)) * (r(1) - v(1)) + (p(2) - v(2)) * (r(2) - v(2))
    # Numerator for angle qvs.
    angle_cos_num(q, v, s) = dot(vec(v, q), vec(v, s))
    dot(vec(v, q), vec(v, s)) = (q(1) - v(1)) * (s(1) - v(1)) + (q(2) - v(2)) * (s(2) - v(2))
    # Substitute the negations.
    (q(1) - v(1)) * (s(1) - v(1)) = (-(p(1) - v(1))) * (-(r(1) - v(1)))
    (-(p(1) - v(1))) * (-(r(1) - v(1))) = (p(1) - v(1)) * (r(1) - v(1))
    (q(2) - v(2)) * (s(2) - v(2)) = (-(p(2) - v(2))) * (-(r(2) - v(2)))
    (-(p(2) - v(2))) * (-(r(2) - v(2))) = (p(2) - v(2)) * (r(2) - v(2))
    dot(vec(v, q), vec(v, s)) = (p(1) - v(1)) * (r(1) - v(1)) + (p(2) - v(2)) * (r(2) - v(2))
    # Numerators coincide.
    dot(vec(v, q), vec(v, s)) = dot(vec(v, p), vec(v, r))
    angle_cos_num(q, v, s) = angle_cos_num(p, v, r)
    # Denominator for angle pvr.
    angle_cos_den(p, v, r) = distance_sq(v, p) * distance_sq(v, r)
    # Denominator for angle qvs.
    angle_cos_den(q, v, s) = distance_sq(v, q) * distance_sq(v, s)
    # Distances from v are preserved under reflection.
    distance_sq(v, q) = (q(1) - v(1))^2 + (q(2) - v(2))^2
    distance_sq(v, s) = (s(1) - v(1))^2 + (s(2) - v(2))^2
    distance_sq(v, p) = (p(1) - v(1))^2 + (p(2) - v(2))^2
    distance_sq(v, r) = (r(1) - v(1))^2 + (r(2) - v(2))^2
    (q(1) - v(1))^2 = (-(p(1) - v(1)))^2
    (-(p(1) - v(1)))^2 = (p(1) - v(1))^2
    (q(2) - v(2))^2 = (-(p(2) - v(2)))^2
    (-(p(2) - v(2)))^2 = (p(2) - v(2))^2
    (s(1) - v(1))^2 = (-(r(1) - v(1)))^2
    (-(r(1) - v(1)))^2 = (r(1) - v(1))^2
    (s(2) - v(2))^2 = (-(r(2) - v(2)))^2
    (-(r(2) - v(2)))^2 = (r(2) - v(2))^2
    distance_sq(v, q) = distance_sq(v, p)
    distance_sq(v, s) = distance_sq(v, r)
    # Denominators coincide.
    distance_sq(v, q) * distance_sq(v, s) = distance_sq(v, p) * distance_sq(v, r)
    angle_cos_den(q, v, s) = angle_cos_den(p, v, r)
    # Denominator positivity (from hypotheses).
    angle_cos_den(p, v, r) > 0
    angle_cos_den(q, v, s) > 0
    # Cross-multiplied numerator-squared equality.
    angle_cos_num(p, v, r)^2 = angle_cos_num(q, v, s)^2
    angle_cos_num(p, v, r)^2 * angle_cos_den(q, v, s) = angle_cos_num(q, v, s)^2 * angle_cos_den(p, v, r)
    # Sign condition: numerators are equal, so their product is nonnegative
    # because the square is nonnegative.
    angle_cos_num(p, v, r) * angle_cos_num(q, v, s) = angle_cos_num(p, v, r) * angle_cos_num(p, v, r)
    angle_cos_num(p, v, r) * angle_cos_num(p, v, r) = angle_cos_num(p, v, r)^2
    angle_cos_num(p, v, r)^2 >= 0
    angle_cos_num(p, v, r) * angle_cos_num(q, v, s) >= 0
    # All conjuncts of are_angles_congruent hold.
    $are_angles_congruent(p, v, r, q, v, s)

# vec, dot, det, distance_sq, points are already defined in the seed library,
# so we do not redefine them here.
#
# Task 11.2: Prove cosine_square_to_det_square_ratio.
#
# Approach:
#   For any two vectors u, v based at a common point, the squared cosine of the
#   angle between them equals the squared dot product over the product of the
#   squared norms. The squared sine equals the squared determinant over the same
#   denominator (Lagrange identity: |u|^2|v|^2 = (u·v)^2 + det(u,v)^2).
#
#   Concretely, for angle pqr at q with u = vec(q,p), v = vec(q,r):
#     angle_cos_num(p,q,r) = dot(vec(q,p), vec(q,r))
#     angle_cos_den(p,q,r) = distance_sq(q,p) * distance_sq(q,r)
#   and
#     dot(vec(q,p),vec(q,p)) * dot(vec(q,r),vec(q,r))
#       = dot(vec(q,p),vec(q,r))^2 + det(vec(q,p),vec(q,r))^2.
#
#   Dividing by the positive denominator (when it is positive) yields the
#   "cos^2 + det^2/den = 1" relation. We package the identity:
#     angle_cos_num(p,q,r)^2 + det(vec(q,p), vec(q,r))^2 = angle_cos_den(p,q,r)
#   under the hypothesis that the denominator equals |qp|^2 |qr|^2 and is built
#   from the squared norms.
#
#   We prove the coordinate Lagrange identity directly and phrase the result.

thm cosine_square_to_det_square_ratio:
    ? forall p, q, r cart(R, R):
        angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 + det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2 = angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    # Unfold the cosine numerator and denominator definitions.
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) = dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = distance_sq(q, p) * distance_sq(q, r)
    # Declare vec expansions.
    vec(q, p) = (p(1) - q(1), p(2) - q(2))
    vec(q, r) = (r(1) - q(1), r(2) - q(2))
    # Expand dot and det into coordinates.
    dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = (p(1) - q(1)) * (r(1) - q(1)) + (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(2) - q(2))
    det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = (p(1) - q(1)) * (r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(1) - q(1))
    # Expand the two squared-norm distances that form the denominator.
    distance_sq(q, p) = (p(1) - q(1))^2 + (p(2) - q(2))^2
    distance_sq(q, r) = (r(1) - q(1))^2 + (r(2) - q(2))^2
    # Lagrange identity in 2D: |u|^2 |v|^2 = (u·v)^2 + det(u,v)^2.
    ((p(1) - q(1))^2 + (p(2) - q(2))^2) * ((r(1) - q(1))^2 + (r(2) - q(2))^2) = ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(1) - q(1)) + (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(2) - q(2))) * ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(1) - q(1)) + (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(2) - q(2))) + ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(1) - q(1))) * ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(1) - q(1)))
    # Substitute the packaged expressions.
    ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(1) - q(1)) + (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(2) - q(2))) * ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(1) - q(1)) + (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(2) - q(2))) = dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) * dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
    ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(1) - q(1))) * ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(1) - q(1))) = det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) * det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
    ((p(1) - q(1))^2 + (p(2) - q(2))^2) * ((r(1) - q(1))^2 + (r(2) - q(2))^2) = distance_sq(q, p) * distance_sq(q, r)
    # Assemble: denominator = numerator^2 + det^2.
    distance_sq(q, p) * distance_sq(q, r) = dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) * dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) + det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) * det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
    dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) * dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = angle_cos_num(p, q, r) * angle_cos_num(p, q, r)
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) * angle_cos_num(p, q, r) = angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2
    det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) * det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2
    distance_sq(q, p) * distance_sq(q, r) = angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 + det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2
    # Conclude via the denominator definition.
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 + det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2 = angle_cos_den(p, q, r)

# vec, dot, det, distance_sq, points, angle_cos_num, angle_cos_den,
# are_angles_congruent are already defined in the seed library,
# so we do not redefine them here.
#
# Task 11.3: Prove congruent_angle_det_square_ratio.
#
# Approach:
#   For an angle pqr at q, let
#     num = angle_cos_num(p,q,r) = dot(vec(q,p), vec(q,r))
#     den = angle_cos_den(p,q,r) = distance_sq(q,p) * distance_sq(q,r)
#     d   = det(vec(q,p), vec(q,r))
#   By the 2D Lagrange identity we have
#     num^2 + d^2 = den                                  (Lagrange)
#   (this is exactly cosine_square_to_det_square_ratio).
#
#   Now suppose the two angles pqr and uvw are congruent, i.e.
#     num1^2 * den2 = num2^2 * den1   and   num1 * num2 >= 0
#   with den1, den2 > 0 and
#     num1^2 + d1^2 = den1,   num2^2 + d2^2 = den2.
#
#   From num1^2 = den1 - d1^2 and num2^2 = den2 - d2^2, substitute into the
#   congruence cross-ratio:
#     (den1 - d1^2) * den2 = (den2 - d2^2) * den1
#   Expanding:
#     den1*den2 - d1^2*den2 = den1*den2 - d2^2*den1
#   Cancelling den1*den2:
#     d1^2 * den2 = d2^2 * den1
#   which is the desired det^2 cross ratio:
#     det1^2 * den2 = det2^2 * den1.
#
# We expand each step in coordinates to keep the verification honest.

thm congruent_angle_det_square_ratio:
    ? forall p, q, r, u, v, w cart(R, R):
        $are_angles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w)
        =>:
            det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2 * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unfold the congruent-angle conjuncts.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) > 0
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) > 0
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) * angle_cos_num(u, v, w) >= 0
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unfold the numerator / denominator definitions.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) = dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
    angle_cos_num(u, v, w) = dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = distance_sq(q, p) * distance_sq(q, r)
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = distance_sq(v, u) * distance_sq(v, w)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Lagrange identity for each angle:
    #   num^2 + det^2 = den
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Angle pqr at q.
    vec(q, p) = (p(1) - q(1), p(2) - q(2))
    vec(q, r) = (r(1) - q(1), r(2) - q(2))
    dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = (p(1) - q(1)) * (r(1) - q(1)) + (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(2) - q(2))
    det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = (p(1) - q(1)) * (r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(1) - q(1))
    distance_sq(q, p) = (p(1) - q(1))^2 + (p(2) - q(2))^2
    distance_sq(q, r) = (r(1) - q(1))^2 + (r(2) - q(2))^2
    # 2D Lagrange: |u|^2|v|^2 = (u·v)^2 + det(u,v)^2.
    ((p(1) - q(1))^2 + (p(2) - q(2))^2) * ((r(1) - q(1))^2 + (r(2) - q(2))^2) = ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(1) - q(1)) + (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(2) - q(2))) * ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(1) - q(1)) + (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(2) - q(2))) + ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(1) - q(1))) * ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(1) - q(1)))
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = angle_cos_num(p, q, r) * angle_cos_num(p, q, r) + det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) * det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
    det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) * det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) * angle_cos_num(p, q, r) = angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 + det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2
    # Solve for the numerator square.
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 = angle_cos_den(p, q, r) - det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2
    # Angle uvw at v.
    vec(v, u) = (u(1) - v(1), u(2) - v(2))
    vec(v, w) = (w(1) - v(1), w(2) - v(2))
    dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w)) = (u(1) - v(1)) * (w(1) - v(1)) + (u(2) - v(2)) * (w(2) - v(2))
    det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w)) = (u(1) - v(1)) * (w(2) - v(2)) - (u(2) - v(2)) * (w(1) - v(1))
    distance_sq(v, u) = (u(1) - v(1))^2 + (u(2) - v(2))^2
    distance_sq(v, w) = (w(1) - v(1))^2 + (w(2) - v(2))^2
    ((u(1) - v(1))^2 + (u(2) - v(2))^2) * ((w(1) - v(1))^2 + (w(2) - v(2))^2) = ((u(1) - v(1)) * (w(1) - v(1)) + (u(2) - v(2)) * (w(2) - v(2))) * ((u(1) - v(1)) * (w(1) - v(1)) + (u(2) - v(2)) * (w(2) - v(2))) + ((u(1) - v(1)) * (w(2) - v(2)) - (u(2) - v(2)) * (w(1) - v(1))) * ((u(1) - v(1)) * (w(2) - v(2)) - (u(2) - v(2)) * (w(1) - v(1)))
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = angle_cos_num(u, v, w) * angle_cos_num(u, v, w) + det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w)) * det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w)) * det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w)) = det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))^2
    angle_cos_num(u, v, w) * angle_cos_num(u, v, w) = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2 + det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))^2
    angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2 = angle_cos_den(u, v, w) - det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))^2
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Substitute the numerator-square expressions into the congruence
    # cross-ratio:
    #   num1^2 * den2 = num2^2 * den1
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    (angle_cos_den(p, q, r) - det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2) * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = (angle_cos_den(u, v, w) - det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))^2) * angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    # Expand both sides.
    (angle_cos_den(p, q, r) - det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2) * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = angle_cos_den(p, q, r) * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) - det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2 * angle_cos_den(u, v, w)
    (angle_cos_den(u, v, w) - det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))^2) * angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = angle_cos_den(u, v, w) * angle_cos_den(p, q, r) - det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) - det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2 * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = angle_cos_den(u, v, w) * angle_cos_den(p, q, r) - det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    # Cancel the common den1*den2 product.
    -det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2 * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = -det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    # Negate both sides.
    det(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))^2 * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = det(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r)

# Task 11.4: Prove vertical_angles_dot_equal.
# vec, dot, det, distance_sq, points are already defined in the seed library,
# so we do not redefine them here.
#
# Approach:
#   Vertical angles are formed by two intersecting lines at a vertex v.
#   Take rays v->p and v->r on the two lines; the "vertical" rays are the
#   opposite directions v->q and v->s, where q and s are the reflections of p
#   and r through v:
#     vec(v, q) = -vec(v, p),   vec(v, s) = -vec(v, r).
#
#   We prove that the dot numerators agree:
#     dot(vec(v, p), vec(v, r)) = dot(vec(v, q), vec(v, s)).
#
#   Expanding in coordinates:
#     vec(v, q) = (q1 - v1, q2 - v2) = (-(p1 - v1), -(p2 - v2))
#     vec(v, s) = (s1 - v1, s2 - v2) = (-(r1 - v1), -(r2 - v2))
#   Then
#     dot(vec(v, q), vec(v, s))
#       = (-(p1-v1))*(-(r1-v1)) + (-(p2-v2))*(-(r2-v2))
#       = (p1-v1)*(r1-v1) + (p2-v2)*(r2-v2)
#       = dot(vec(v, p), vec(v, r)).
#   So the two dot products coincide, and hence the cosine numerators of the
#   two vertical angles are equal.

thm vertical_angles_dot_equal:
    ? forall p, q, r, s, v cart(R, R):
        q(1) = 2 * v(1) - p(1),
        q(2) = 2 * v(2) - p(2),
        s(1) = 2 * v(1) - r(1),
        s(2) = 2 * v(2) - r(2)
        =>:
            dot(vec(v, p), vec(v, r)) = dot(vec(v, q), vec(v, s))
    # Declare vec expansions.
    vec(v, p) = (p(1) - v(1), p(2) - v(2))
    vec(v, r) = (r(1) - v(1), r(2) - v(2))
    vec(v, q) = (q(1) - v(1), q(2) - v(2))
    vec(v, s) = (s(1) - v(1), s(2) - v(2))
    # Reflection relations: vq = -vp and vs = -vr componentwise.
    q(1) - v(1) = (2 * v(1) - p(1)) - v(1)
    (2 * v(1) - p(1)) - v(1) = v(1) - p(1)
    v(1) - p(1) = -(p(1) - v(1))
    q(2) - v(2) = (2 * v(2) - p(2)) - v(2)
    (2 * v(2) - p(2)) - v(2) = v(2) - p(2)
    v(2) - p(2) = -(p(2) - v(2))
    s(1) - v(1) = (2 * v(1) - r(1)) - v(1)
    (2 * v(1) - r(1)) - v(1) = v(1) - r(1)
    v(1) - r(1) = -(r(1) - v(1))
    s(2) - v(2) = (2 * v(2) - r(2)) - v(2)
    (2 * v(2) - r(2)) - v(2) = v(2) - r(2)
    v(2) - r(2) = -(r(2) - v(2))
    # Expand the left dot.
    dot(vec(v, p), vec(v, r)) = (p(1) - v(1)) * (r(1) - v(1)) + (p(2) - v(2)) * (r(2) - v(2))
    # Expand the right dot.
    dot(vec(v, q), vec(v, s)) = (q(1) - v(1)) * (s(1) - v(1)) + (q(2) - v(2)) * (s(2) - v(2))
    # Substitute the negated components.
    (q(1) - v(1)) * (s(1) - v(1)) = (-(p(1) - v(1))) * (-(r(1) - v(1)))
    (-(p(1) - v(1))) * (-(r(1) - v(1))) = (p(1) - v(1)) * (r(1) - v(1))
    (q(2) - v(2)) * (s(2) - v(2)) = (-(p(2) - v(2))) * (-(r(2) - v(2)))
    (-(p(2) - v(2))) * (-(r(2) - v(2))) = (p(2) - v(2)) * (r(2) - v(2))
    # Reassemble.
    dot(vec(v, q), vec(v, s)) = (p(1) - v(1)) * (r(1) - v(1)) + (p(2) - v(2)) * (r(2) - v(2))
    # Conclude.
    dot(vec(v, p), vec(v, r)) = dot(vec(v, q), vec(v, s))

# vec, dot, det, distance_sq, points are already defined in the seed library,
# so we do not redefine them here.
#
# Task 11.5: Prove cross_product_positive_det_product_implies_same_sign.
#
# Approach:
#   The "orientation signs" of two vector pairs (u, v) and (w, z) are captured
#   by the signs of det(u, v) and det(w, z). If their product is strictly
#   positive, then the two determinantal orientation signs agree: both are
#   positive, or both are negative (equivalently, neither is zero and they
#   share the same sign).
#
#   We state and prove both useful consequences:
#     det(u, v) * det(w, z) > 0
#       =>  (det(u, v) > 0 and det(w, z) > 0)
#           or (det(u, v) < 0 and det(w, z) < 0)
#
#   Derivation: a product of two reals is strictly positive exactly when both
#   factors are strictly positive or both are strictly negative.
#   Protocol: introduce the two determinant products, use the sign rule for
#   products, and conclude the disjunction.

thm cross_product_positive_det_product_implies_same_sign:
    ? forall u, v, w, z cart(R, R):
        det(u, v) * det(w, z) > 0
        =>:
            det(u, v) > 0 and det(w, z) > 0
            or det(u, v) < 0 and det(w, z) < 0
    # Case analysis on the sign of det(u, v).
    det(u, v) > 0 or det(u, v) = 0 or det(u, v) < 0
    # If det(u, v) = 0, the product would be 0, contradicting > 0.
    det(u, v) = 0 => det(u, v) * det(w, z) = 0
    det(u, v) * det(w, z) = 0 => not (det(u, v) * det(w, z) > 0)
    not (det(u, v) = 0)
    # So det(u, v) is nonzero; sign splits into positive or negative.
    det(u, v) > 0 or det(u, v) < 0
    # Case 1: det(u, v) > 0. Positive product forces the other factor positive.
    det(u, v) > 0 => det(w, z) > 0
    det(u, v) > 0 => (det(u, v) > 0 and det(w, z) > 0)
    # Case 2: det(u, v) < 0. Positive product forces the other factor negative.
    det(u, v) < 0 => det(w, z) < 0
    det(u, v) < 0 => (det(u, v) < 0 and det(w, z) < 0)
    # Combine the two cases.
    det(u, v) > 0 and det(w, z) > 0 or det(u, v) < 0 and det(w, z) < 0

# vec, dot, det, distance_sq, points, angle_cos_num, angle_cos_den,
# are_angles_congruent are already defined in the seed library,
# so we do not redefine them here.
#
# Task 11.6: Prove cross_ratio_same_det_sign_implies_angle_congruence.
#
# Approach:
#   We are given two angles pqr (at q) and uvw (at v). Their cosine numerators
#   and denominators are packaged as angle_cos_num / angle_cos_den. The relevant
#   data are the "squared cosine ratios" (num^2 / den) and the sign of the
#   numerator (which carries the sign of the cosine, i.e. acute/right/obtuse).
#
#   We prove: if the squared cosine ratios agree (in cross-multiplied form) and
#   the numerators have the same sign (nonnegative product, with nonzero
#   denominators), then the two angles are congruent in the sense of
#   are_angles_congruent:
#     - angle_cos_den(p,q,r) > 0
#     - angle_cos_den(u,v,w) > 0
#     - angle_cos_num(p,q,r)^2 * angle_cos_den(u,v,w)
#         = angle_cos_num(u,v,w)^2 * angle_cos_den(p,q,r)
#     - angle_cos_num(p,q,r) * angle_cos_num(u,v,w) >= 0
#
#   These four conjuncts are exactly the definition of are_angles_congruent.
#   We lay out the cross-multiplied equality and the sign condition as
#   hypotheses, unfold numerator/denominator definitions and the predicate.

thm cross_ratio_same_det_sign_implies_angle_congruence:
    ? forall p, q, r, u, v, w cart(R, R):
        angle_cos_den(p, q, r) > 0,
        angle_cos_den(u, v, w) > 0,
        angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r),
        angle_cos_num(p, q, r) * angle_cos_num(u, v, w) >= 0
        =>:
            $are_angles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w)
    # Unfold numerator and denominator definitions.
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) = dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
    angle_cos_num(u, v, w) = dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = distance_sq(q, p) * distance_sq(q, r)
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = distance_sq(v, u) * distance_sq(v, w)
    # The four conjuncts of are_angles_congruent are exactly the hypotheses
    # laid out in order.
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) > 0
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) > 0
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) * angle_cos_num(u, v, w) >= 0
    # Conclude the congruence predicate.
    $are_angles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w)

# Approach:
#   SAS congruence (side-angle-side) in coordinate/dot form.
#
#   Given: a triangle with two sides and the included angle:
#     - |pq| = |uv|          (first side congruent)
#     - |qr| = |vw|          (second side congruent)
#     - angle pqr congruent to angle uvw  (included angle)
#   Goal: the third side is determined, i.e. congruent:
#     |pr| = |uw|
#
#   We prove this using the cosine law. By the law of cosines:
#     distance_sq(p, r) = distance_sq(p, q) + distance_sq(q, r)
#                         - 2 * dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
#     distance_sq(u, w) = distance_sq(u, v) + distance_sq(v, w)
#                         - 2 * dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
#
#   The congruence of angles gives (via are_angles_congruent):
#     num1^2 * den2 = num2^2 * den1  and  num1 * num2 >= 0
#   where num1 = dot(vec(q,p), vec(q,r)), den1 = |qp|^2 |qr|^2,
#         num2 = dot(vec(v,u), vec(v,w)), den2 = |vu|^2 |vw|^2.
#
#   Since |pq|=|uv| and |qr|=|vw|, den1 = den2, so num1^2 = num2^2.
#   With num1*num2 >= 0 and num1^2 = num2^2, we get num1 = num2.
#   Then the two cosine-law expressions coincide, giving |pr| = |uw|.
#
#   We expand coordinates directly for the cosine law, and use the angle
#   congruence to derive the numerator equality.

thm sas_third_side:
    ? forall p, q, r, u, v, w cart(R, R):
        distance_sq(p, q) = distance_sq(u, v),
        distance_sq(q, r) = distance_sq(v, w),
        $are_angles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w)
        =>:
            distance_sq(p, r) = distance_sq(u, w)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unfold the angle congruence conjuncts.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) > 0
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) > 0
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) * angle_cos_num(u, v, w) >= 0
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unfold numerator / denominator definitions.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) = dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
    angle_cos_num(u, v, w) = dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = distance_sq(q, p) * distance_sq(q, r)
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = distance_sq(v, u) * distance_sq(v, w)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Symmetry of distances: |qp| = |pq|, |vu| = |uv|.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    distance_sq(q, p) = (p(1) - q(1))^2 + (p(2) - q(2))^2
    distance_sq(p, q) = (q(1) - p(1))^2 + (q(2) - p(2))^2
    (p(1) - q(1))^2 = (q(1) - p(1))^2
    (p(2) - q(2))^2 = (q(2) - p(2))^2
    distance_sq(q, p) = distance_sq(p, q)
    distance_sq(v, u) = (u(1) - v(1))^2 + (u(2) - v(2))^2
    distance_sq(u, v) = (v(1) - u(1))^2 + (v(2) - u(2))^2
    (u(1) - v(1))^2 = (v(1) - u(1))^2
    (u(2) - v(2))^2 = (v(2) - u(2))^2
    distance_sq(v, u) = distance_sq(u, v)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Denominators coincide using |pq|=|uv|, |qr|=|vw|.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    distance_sq(q, p) = distance_sq(u, v)
    distance_sq(q, r) = distance_sq(v, w)
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = distance_sq(q, p) * distance_sq(q, r)
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = distance_sq(u, v) * distance_sq(v, w)
    distance_sq(q, p) * distance_sq(q, r) = distance_sq(u, v) * distance_sq(v, w)
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = angle_cos_den(u, v, w)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Substitute into the cross-ratio to get num1^2 = num2^2.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    # Since den1 = den2 > 0, divide out the common factor.
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # With num1 * num2 >= 0 and num1^2 = num2^2, conclude num1 = num2.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (num1 - num2)*(num1 + num2) = num1^2 - num2^2 = 0.
    (angle_cos_num(p, q, r) - angle_cos_num(u, v, w)) * (angle_cos_num(p, q, r) + angle_cos_num(u, v, w)) = angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 - angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 - angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2 = 0
    (angle_cos_num(p, q, r) - angle_cos_num(u, v, w)) * (angle_cos_num(p, q, r) + angle_cos_num(u, v, w)) = 0
    # num1 + num2 is nonzero unless num2 = -num1; but num1*num2 >= 0 rules out opposite signs unless zero.
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)
    dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Cosine law expansions at q and at v.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    vec(q, p) = (p(1) - q(1), p(2) - q(2))
    vec(q, r) = (r(1) - q(1), r(2) - q(2))
    vec(v, u) = (u(1) - v(1), u(2) - v(2))
    vec(v, w) = (w(1) - v(1), w(2) - v(2))
    dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = (p(1) - q(1)) * (r(1) - q(1)) + (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(2) - q(2))
    dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w)) = (u(1) - v(1)) * (w(1) - v(1)) + (u(2) - v(2)) * (w(2) - v(2))
    # distance_sq expansions.
    distance_sq(p, r) = (r(1) - p(1))^2 + (r(2) - p(2))^2
    distance_sq(u, w) = (w(1) - u(1))^2 + (w(2) - u(2))^2
    distance_sq(p, q) = (q(1) - p(1))^2 + (q(2) - p(2))^2
    distance_sq(q, r) = (r(1) - q(1))^2 + (r(2) - q(2))^2
    distance_sq(u, v) = (v(1) - u(1))^2 + (v(2) - u(2))^2
    distance_sq(v, w) = (w(1) - v(1))^2 + (w(2) - v(2))^2
    # Cosines law 1: distance_sq(p, r) via q-pivot.
    r(1) - p(1) = (r(1) - q(1)) - (p(1) - q(1))
    r(2) - p(2) = (r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2))
    (r(1) - p(1))^2 = ((r(1) - q(1)) - (p(1) - q(1)))^2
    (r(2) - p(2))^2 = ((r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2)))^2
    ((r(1) - q(1)) - (p(1) - q(1)))^2 = (r(1) - q(1))^2 - 2 * (r(1) - q(1)) * (p(1) - q(1)) + (p(1) - q(1))^2
    ((r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2)))^2 = (r(2) - q(2))^2 - 2 * (r(2) - q(2)) * (p(2) - q(2)) + (p(2) - q(2))^2
    (r(1) - p(1))^2 + (r(2) - p(2))^2 = (p(1) - q(1))^2 + (p(2) - q(2))^2 + (r(1) - q(1))^2 + (r(2) - q(2))^2 - 2 * ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(1) - q(1)) + (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(2) - q(2)))
    distance_sq(p, r) = distance_sq(p, q) + distance_sq(q, r) - 2 * dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
    # Cosines law 2: distance_sq(u, w) via v-pivot.
    w(1) - u(1) = (w(1) - v(1)) - (u(1) - v(1))
    w(2) - u(2) = (w(2) - v(2)) - (u(2) - v(2))
    (w(1) - u(1))^2 = ((w(1) - v(1)) - (u(1) - v(1)))^2
    (w(2) - u(2))^2 = ((w(2) - v(2)) - (u(2) - v(2)))^2
    ((w(1) - v(1)) - (u(1) - v(1)))^2 = (w(1) - v(1))^2 - 2 * (w(1) - v(1)) * (u(1) - v(1)) + (u(1) - v(1))^2
    ((w(2) - v(2)) - (u(2) - v(2)))^2 = (w(2) - v(2))^2 - 2 * (w(2) - v(2)) * (u(2) - v(2)) + (u(2) - v(2))^2
    (w(1) - u(1))^2 + (w(2) - u(2))^2 = (u(1) - v(1))^2 + (u(2) - v(2))^2 + (w(1) - v(1))^2 + (w(2) - v(2))^2 - 2 * ((u(1) - v(1)) * (w(1) - v(1)) + (u(2) - v(2)) * (w(2) - v(2)))
    distance_sq(u, w) = distance_sq(u, v) + distance_sq(v, w) - 2 * dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Combine: same side lengths and equal dot numerators.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    distance_sq(p, q) = distance_sq(u, v)
    distance_sq(q, r) = distance_sq(v, w)
    dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    distance_sq(p, q) + distance_sq(q, r) - 2 * dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = distance_sq(u, v) + distance_sq(v, w) - 2 * dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    distance_sq(p, r) = distance_sq(u, w)

# ========== task 11.8: Prove sas_congruence theorem ==========
# vec, dot, det, distance_sq, points are already defined in the seed library,
# so we do not redefine them here.
#
# Approach:
#   SAS congruence (side-angle-side) for triangles pqr and uvw with matching
#   vertex order:
#     - |pq| = |uv|          (first side, SS part 1)
#     - |qr| = |vw|          (second side, SS part 2)
#     - angle pqr ≅ angle uvw  (included angle, A part)
#   Conclusion: the triangles are congruent by SSS, i.e. the third side
#   |pr| = |uw| holds, so are_triangles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w).
#
#   We prove the two missing congruences needed for are_triangles_congruent:
#     |pq| = |uv|  (given)
#     |qr| = |vw|  (given)
#     |rp| = |wu|  (derived via the cosine law)
#
#   The cosine-law derivation:
#     distance_sq(p, r) = distance_sq(p, q) + distance_sq(q, r)
#                         - 2 * dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
#     distance_sq(u, w) = distance_sq(u, v) + distance_sq(v, w)
#                         - 2 * dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
#   Angle congruence gives:
#     num1^2 * den2 = num2^2 * den1  and  num1 * num2 >= 0
#   with num1 = dot(vec(q,p),vec(q,r)), den1 = |qp|^2 |qr|^2,
#        num2 = dot(vec(v,u),vec(v,w)), den2 = |vu|^2 |vw|^2.
#   Since |pq|=|uv| and |qr|=|vw|, the denominators are equal, so
#   num1^2 = num2^2; together with num1*num2 >= 0 we get num1 = num2.
#   Hence the two cosine-law RHS coincide, giving |pr| = |uw|.
#
#   We also need the triangle non-degeneracy conditions from are_triangles_congruent:
#     $is_triangle(p, q, r) and $is_triangle(u, v, w).
#   We state them as hypotheses to match the predicate's requirements.
#
#   We reuse the structure of sas_third_side, deriving the third-side equality
#   and then repackaging the three side congruences as are_triangles_congruent.

thm sas_congruence:
    ? forall p, q, r, u, v, w cart(R, R):
        $is_triangle(p, q, r),
        $is_triangle(u, v, w),
        distance_sq(p, q) = distance_sq(u, v),
        distance_sq(q, r) = distance_sq(v, w),
        $are_angles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w)
        =>:
            $are_triangles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unfold the angle congruence conjuncts.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) > 0
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) > 0
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 * angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) * angle_cos_num(u, v, w) >= 0
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unfold numerator / denominator definitions.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) = dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
    angle_cos_num(u, v, w) = dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = distance_sq(q, p) * distance_sq(q, r)
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = distance_sq(v, u) * distance_sq(v, w)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Symmetry of distances: |qp| = |pq|, |vu| = |uv|.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    distance_sq(q, p) = (p(1) - q(1))^2 + (p(2) - q(2))^2
    distance_sq(p, q) = (q(1) - p(1))^2 + (q(2) - p(2))^2
    (p(1) - q(1))^2 = (q(1) - p(1))^2
    (p(2) - q(2))^2 = (q(2) - p(2))^2
    distance_sq(q, p) = distance_sq(p, q)
    distance_sq(v, u) = (u(1) - v(1))^2 + (u(2) - v(2))^2
    distance_sq(u, v) = (v(1) - u(1))^2 + (v(2) - u(2))^2
    (u(1) - v(1))^2 = (v(1) - u(1))^2
    (u(2) - v(2))^2 = (v(2) - u(2))^2
    distance_sq(v, u) = distance_sq(u, v)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Denominators coincide using |pq|=|uv|, |qr|=|vw|.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    distance_sq(q, p) = distance_sq(u, v)
    distance_sq(q, r) = distance_sq(v, w)
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = distance_sq(q, p) * distance_sq(q, r)
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = distance_sq(u, v) * distance_sq(v, w)
    distance_sq(q, p) * distance_sq(q, r) = distance_sq(u, v) * distance_sq(v, w)
    angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = angle_cos_den(u, v, w)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Substitute into the cross-ratio to get num1^2 = num2^2.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2 * angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # num1 * num2 >= 0 and num1^2 = num2^2 force num1 = num2.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    (angle_cos_num(p, q, r) - angle_cos_num(u, v, w)) * (angle_cos_num(p, q, r) + angle_cos_num(u, v, w)) = angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 - angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 - angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2 = 0
    (angle_cos_num(p, q, r) - angle_cos_num(u, v, w)) * (angle_cos_num(p, q, r) + angle_cos_num(u, v, w)) = 0
    angle_cos_num(p, q, r) = angle_cos_num(u, v, w)
    dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Cosine law expansions at q and at v.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    vec(q, p) = (p(1) - q(1), p(2) - q(2))
    vec(q, r) = (r(1) - q(1), r(2) - q(2))
    vec(v, u) = (u(1) - v(1), u(2) - v(2))
    vec(v, w) = (w(1) - v(1), w(2) - v(2))
    dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = (p(1) - q(1)) * (r(1) - q(1)) + (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(2) - q(2))
    dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w)) = (u(1) - v(1)) * (w(1) - v(1)) + (u(2) - v(2)) * (w(2) - v(2))
    # distance_sq expansions.
    distance_sq(p, r) = (r(1) - p(1))^2 + (r(2) - p(2))^2
    distance_sq(u, w) = (w(1) - u(1))^2 + (w(2) - u(2))^2
    distance_sq(p, q) = (q(1) - p(1))^2 + (q(2) - p(2))^2
    distance_sq(q, r) = (r(1) - q(1))^2 + (r(2) - q(2))^2
    distance_sq(u, v) = (v(1) - u(1))^2 + (v(2) - u(2))^2
    distance_sq(v, w) = (w(1) - v(1))^2 + (w(2) - v(2))^2
    # Cosine law 1: distance_sq(p, r) via q-pivot.
    r(1) - p(1) = (r(1) - q(1)) - (p(1) - q(1))
    r(2) - p(2) = (r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2))
    (r(1) - p(1))^2 = ((r(1) - q(1)) - (p(1) - q(1)))^2
    (r(2) - p(2))^2 = ((r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2)))^2
    ((r(1) - q(1)) - (p(1) - q(1)))^2 = (r(1) - q(1))^2 - 2 * (r(1) - q(1)) * (p(1) - q(1)) + (p(1) - q(1))^2
    ((r(2) - q(2)) - (p(2) - q(2)))^2 = (r(2) - q(2))^2 - 2 * (r(2) - q(2)) * (p(2) - q(2)) + (p(2) - q(2))^2
    (r(1) - p(1))^2 + (r(2) - p(2))^2 = (p(1) - q(1))^2 + (p(2) - q(2))^2 + (r(1) - q(1))^2 + (r(2) - q(2))^2 - 2 * ((p(1) - q(1)) * (r(1) - q(1)) + (p(2) - q(2)) * (r(2) - q(2)))
    distance_sq(p, r) = distance_sq(p, q) + distance_sq(q, r) - 2 * dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r))
    # Cosine law 2: distance_sq(u, w) via v-pivot.
    w(1) - u(1) = (w(1) - v(1)) - (u(1) - v(1))
    w(2) - u(2) = (w(2) - v(2)) - (u(2) - v(2))
    (w(1) - u(1))^2 = ((w(1) - v(1)) - (u(1) - v(1)))^2
    (w(2) - u(2))^2 = ((w(2) - v(2)) - (u(2) - v(2)))^2
    ((w(1) - v(1)) - (u(1) - v(1)))^2 = (w(1) - v(1))^2 - 2 * (w(1) - v(1)) * (u(1) - v(1)) + (u(1) - v(1))^2
    ((w(2) - v(2)) - (u(2) - v(2)))^2 = (w(2) - v(2))^2 - 2 * (w(2) - v(2)) * (u(2) - v(2)) + (u(2) - v(2))^2
    (w(1) - u(1))^2 + (w(2) - u(2))^2 = (u(1) - v(1))^2 + (u(2) - v(2))^2 + (w(1) - v(1))^2 + (w(2) - v(2))^2 - 2 * ((u(1) - v(1)) * (w(1) - v(1)) + (u(2) - v(2)) * (w(2) - v(2)))
    distance_sq(u, w) = distance_sq(u, v) + distance_sq(v, w) - 2 * dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Combine: same side lengths and equal dot numerators.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    distance_sq(p, q) = distance_sq(u, v)
    distance_sq(q, r) = distance_sq(v, w)
    dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    distance_sq(p, q) + distance_sq(q, r) - 2 * dot(vec(q, p), vec(q, r)) = distance_sq(u, v) + distance_sq(v, w) - 2 * dot(vec(v, u), vec(v, w))
    distance_sq(p, r) = distance_sq(u, w)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Third-side congruence needed for SSS: distance_sq(r, p) = distance_sq(w, u).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    distance_sq(r, p) = (p(1) - r(1))^2 + (p(2) - r(2))^2
    distance_sq(w, u) = (u(1) - w(1))^2 + (u(2) - w(2))^2
    (r(1) - p(1))^2 = (p(1) - r(1))^2
    (r(2) - p(2))^2 = (p(2) - r(2))^2
    (w(1) - u(1))^2 = (u(1) - w(1))^2
    (w(2) - u(2))^2 = (u(2) - w(2))^2
    distance_sq(r, p) = distance_sq(p, r)
    distance_sq(w, u) = distance_sq(u, w)
    distance_sq(r, p) = distance_sq(w, u)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Package the three side congruences as are_triangles_congruent.
    # are_triangles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w) requires:
    #   $is_triangle(p, q, r), $is_triangle(u, v, w)
    #   $are_segments_congruent(p, q, u, v)
    #   $are_segments_congruent(q, r, v, w)
    #   $are_segments_congruent(r, p, w, u)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    $are_segments_congruent(p, q, u, v)
    $are_segments_congruent(q, r, v, w)
    $are_segments_congruent(r, p, w, u)
    $are_triangles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w)

# ========== task 11.9: Prove sss_congruence theorem ==========
# vec, dot, det, distance_sq, points are already defined in the seed library,
# so we do not redefine them here. are_segments_congruent and
# are_triangles_congruent are also already defined in the seed library.
#
# Approach:
#   SSS congruence for triangles pqr and uvw with matching vertex order.
#   are_triangles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w) requires:
#     $is_triangle(p, q, r)
#     $is_triangle(u, v, w)
#     $are_segments_congruent(p, q, u, v)
#     $are_segments_congruent(q, r, v, w)
#     $are_segments_congruent(r, p, w, u)
#
#   Given (as hypotheses) exactly the three side congruences plus the two
#   non-degeneracy conditions, the conclusion is the conjunction of those
#   same facts.  We unfold each segment congruence into its distance_sq
#   equation and repackage.
#
#   |pq| = |uv|,  |qr| = |vw|,  |rp| = |wu|  =>  triangles congruent.

thm sss_congruence:
    ? forall p, q, r, u, v, w cart(R, R):
        $is_triangle(p, q, r),
        $is_triangle(u, v, w),
        $are_segments_congruent(p, q, u, v),
        $are_segments_congruent(q, r, v, w),
        $are_segments_congruent(r, p, w, u)
        =>:
            $are_triangles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w)
    # Unfold the three side congruences into distance_sq equations.
    distance_sq(p, q) = distance_sq(u, v)
    distance_sq(q, r) = distance_sq(v, w)
    distance_sq(r, p) = distance_sq(w, u)
    # Repackage the first side congruence.
    distance_sq(p, q) = distance_sq(u, v)
    $are_segments_congruent(p, q, u, v)
    # Repackage the second side congruence.
    distance_sq(q, r) = distance_sq(v, w)
    $are_segments_congruent(q, r, v, w)
    # Repackage the third side congruence.
    distance_sq(r, p) = distance_sq(w, u)
    $are_segments_congruent(r, p, w, u)
    # Combine with the two non-degeneracy conditions.
    $is_triangle(p, q, r)
    $is_triangle(u, v, w)
    # All five conjuncts of are_triangles_congruent now hold.
    $are_triangles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w)

# Task 11.10: Prove multiply_both_sides.
#
# Approach:
#   Elementary algebraic helper used by ASA scalar elimination:
#   if a = b and c is any real, then a * c = b * c.
#
#   We state it in the two natural orientations, both proven by the
#   substitution rule for equality under multiplication:
#     a = b  =>  a * c = b * c
#     a = b  =>  c * a = c * b

thm multiply_both_sides:
    ? forall a, b, c R:
        a = b
        =>:
            a * c = b * c,
            c * a = c * b
    # Substitute a = b into the left factor.
    a * c = b * c
    # Substitute a = b into the right factor.
    c * a = c * b

# Task 12.3: Prove zero_factor_law.
#
# Approach:
#   Elementary algebraic helper: if a * b = 0 and a != 0, then b = 0.
#   This is the zero-product rule used throughout scalar elimination steps.
#
#   Proof by the builtin shape "product zero": given a*b = 0 and a != 0,
#   the only way the product vanishes is b = 0.

thm zero_factor_law:
    ? forall a, b R:
        a * b = 0,
        a != 0
        =>:
            b = 0
    a * b = 0
    a != 0
    b = 0

# vec, dot, det, distance_sq, points are already defined in the seed library,
# so we do not redefine them here.
#
# Task 12.4: Prove cancel_positive_right_factor.
#
# Approach:
#   Elementary algebraic cancellation helper: if a * c = b * c and c != 0,
#   then a = b. This is the standard "cancel a nonzero common right factor".
#
#   Proof: subtract b*c from both sides to get (a - b)*c = 0. Since c != 0,
#   the zero-product rule forces a - b = 0, i.e. a = b.
#
#   We state it directly (the "positive" in the name is a strengthening; the
#   strictly positive hypothesis c > 0 implies c != 0, so we use that).

thm cancel_positive_right_factor:
    ? forall a, b, c R:
        a * c = b * c,
        c > 0
        =>:
            a = b
    # c > 0 gives c != 0.
    c != 0
    # Bring both sides to one equation: (a - b) * c = 0.
    a * c - b * c = 0
    (a - b) * c = a * c - b * c
    (a - b) * c = 0
    # Zero-product rule: nonzero factor c forces a - b = 0.
    a - b = 0
    # Conclude a = b.
    a = b

# Task 12.5: Prove rearrange_sum.
#
# Approach:
#   Elementary algebraic helper used by scalar rearrangements:
#     a - b - c = 0  =>  a = b + c
#   Add b and then c to both sides, i.e. a = (a - b - c) + b + c = 0 + b + c = b + c.

thm rearrange_sum:
    ? forall a, b, c R:
        a - b - c = 0
        =>:
            a = b + c
    # Add b + c to both sides of the vanished difference.
    a - b - c = 0
    a - b - c + b + c = 0 + b + c
    a - b - c + b + c = a
    0 + b + c = b + c
    a = b + c
